name: Treaty with the Wea, 1818
aka: Treaty of St. Mary's with the Wea, October 2, 1818
nations: Wea (now part of the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: A reservation on the Wabash at Raccoon Creek kept for the Wea (Article 2).
One section of land each granted to two named children of the Wea, not to be sold without the President's consent (Article 3).
An added annuity of $1,850, making $3,000 a year in silver, paid on the reservation (Article 5).

breaches.what: For the Wea's interest in Royce Area 99 in Indiana, ceded by Article 1 of this treaty, the Indian Claims Commission had entered an award of $937,250 to the Wea, against which it credited the $34,478.16 the Wea received for that cession and other offsets, leaving a net judgment of $876,477.30. The earlier decision (9 Ind. Cl. Comm. 274, 1961) was affirmed by the Court of Claims (169 Ct. Cl. 1009, 1965).

breaches.what: Article 4 of this treaty gave the Wea's consent to the Kickapoo cession of Royce Area 74 (91,000 acres in the Wabash valley). The Commission valued Area 74 at $1.50 an acre as of 7 January 1819, the date this treaty took effect, and held the consideration for Areas 73 and 74 unconscionable, finding the Wea entitled to $351,750 less $2,000 (Docket 314-C).

landTaken: All Wea lands in Indiana, Ohio and Illinois except the Article 2 reservation (Royce Area 114, 27,330.66 acres), which was ceded in 1820 (see kappler-198).
compensation: Article 5 annuity, the whole Wea consideration for Area 99 credited by the Commission at $34,478.16. Net award of $876,477.30 for Area 99 (1963) and $349,750 under Docket 314-C for Areas 73 and 74 (1970).
today: Royce lists Areas 114 and 74 under this entry; the Area 99 award is recorded here because the Wea ceded their interest in Area 99 by this treaty, although Royce's map places Area 99 under the Miami treaty of 6 October 1818 (kappler-179).

openQuestions: The 1961 decision (9 Ind. Cl. Comm. 274) that set the $937,250 award for Area 99 was not opened; whether it rests on an unconscionable-consideration holding should be confirmed.
A Peoria Tribe statement on this treaty was not found.
